data_window: 2026-08-21 00:00 to 2026-08-24 12:08 Asia/Shanghai. GitHub Search API queries covered `ai agent`, `mcp agent`, `browser agent`, `code agent`, and `AI workflow` with created/pushed windows and sort=stars/updated. Raw responses were saved under `/tmp/radar_2026_08_24_*.json`; selected README audits were saved under `/tmp/radar_2026_08_24_readmes/`.
source_summary: git fetch origin succeeded on `main...origin/main`; pre-existing unrelated frontend/deploy worktree changes and the old untracked `data/runs/2026-08-19-lark-message.md` were preserved unstaged. Discovery used unauthenticated GitHub Search API metadata plus selected README raw downloads. No third-party repository was cloned, installed, built, run, browser-tested, desktop-tested, mobile-tested, MCP-handshake-tested, credential-tested, provider-tested, payment-tested, security-scanned or deployed.
trend_observations: Today’s strongest cluster is agent work becoming operational product infrastructure: parallel coding-agent ADEs, repository-context accelerators, MCP-native design canvases, remote control planes, vertical agent studios, privacy proxies, secrets brokers, proof-of-work skills and credential lifecycle tooling. README evidence for install paths, screenshots, API/MCP surfaces, approvals, threat models and domain-specific workflows mattered more than stars alone.
assumptions: Scores are editorial point-in-time rankings based on GitHub Search API metadata, README evidence, visible product surface, install/build cues, documentation completeness, repository freshness and AI-native workflow depth. Stars/forks are unauthenticated API snapshots, not exact growth deltas. README claims were not independently runtime-verified. Mature platforms, pure collections, proposal repos, generated marketing READMEs, thin wrappers and projects without clear runnable surfaces were downgraded or skipped.
